record.original_question: Let M be a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold whose first Betti number is at least one. Is every even integral second cohomology class a ∈ H 2 (M ; R) of dual Thurston norm one realised as the Euler class of some tight contact structure on M ?

evidence.quote: Question 2.11. Let M be a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold whose first Betti number is at least one. Is every even integral second cohomology class a ∈ H 2 (M ; R) of dual Thurston norm one realised as the Euler class of some tight contact structure on M ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed orientable hyperbolic 3-manifold with first Betti number $b_1(M) \geq 1$. Recall that the Thurston norm $x: H_2(M;\mathbb{R}) \to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ is defined on integral classes by $x(\alpha) = \min\{\sum_i \max(0, -\chi(S_i))\}$, where the minimum is taken over all properly embedded oriented surfaces $S = \bigsqcup_i S_i$ representing $\alpha$ (via Poincaré duality), and extended to $H_2(M;\mathbb{R})$ by continuity and linearity. The dual Thurston norm on $H^2(M;\mathbb{R}) \cong H_1(M;\mathbb{R})$ is defined by
$$x^*(a) = \sup\{\langle a, \alpha\rangle : \alpha \in H_2(M;\mathbb{R}),\ x(\alpha) \leq 1\}.$$
An integral class $a \in H^2(M;\mathbb{Z}) \subset H^2(M;\mathbb{R})$ is called even if it lies in $2\,H^2(M;\mathbb{Z})$. A cooriented 2-plane field $\xi \subset TM$ is a contact structure if $\xi = \ker\alpha$ for a 1-form $\alpha$ with $\alpha\wedge d\alpha \neq 0$ everywhere; its Euler class $e(\xi) \in H^2(M;\mathbb{Z})$ is the Euler class of the oriented plane bundle $\xi$. A contact structure is tight if there is no embedded disk $D \subset M$ along whose boundary $\xi$ is tangent to $D$ while transverse to $D$ in the interior.

Question: Is it true that every even integral class $a \in H^2(M;\mathbb{Z})$ with dual Thurston norm $x^*(a) = 1$ is realized as the Euler class $e(\xi)$ of some tight contact structure $\xi$ on $M$?
artifact.category_tag: tight contact structures and Thurston norm
artifact.status_search_result: The analogue of Thurston's Euler class one conjecture for tight contact structures on hyperbolic 3-manifolds is an active question. Recent work by Sivek (2022/2023) and subsequent papers (e.g., on fillable contact structures, 2024) discuss the problem and show that known counterexamples to the taut-foliation version are nonetheless realized by tight contact structures, but no proof or counterexample for hyperbolic 3-manifolds with $b_1\geq 1$ has been established. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Thurston norm and Euler classes of tight contact structures
status_evidence.snippet: Tight contact structures exist whenever taut foliations do and their Euler classes also have norm at most one, so it is natural to ask whether the Euler class one conjecture might still be true for tight contact structures.
status_evidence.claim: Sivek formulates and studies the Euler class one question for tight contact structures, leaving it open in general.

status_evidence.title: On the Euler class one conjecture for fillable contact structures
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work examines the Euler class one conjecture in the setting of (fillable) contact structures, indicating it remains an active open question.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature continues to treat the conjecture as open.
